questionText:
A given program has $25\%$ load/store instructions. Suppose the ideal CPI (cycles per instruction) without any memory stalls is $2$. The program exhibits $2\%$ miss rate on instruction cache and $8\%$ miss rate on data cache. The miss penalty is $100$ cycles.

The speedup (rounded off to two decimal places) achieved with a perfect cache (i.e., with NO data or instruction cache misses) is ________
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate Instruction Cache Stalls
Instruction miss rate per instruction = $2\% = 0.02$
Instruction cache stall cycles per instruction = $0.02 \times 100 = 2$ cycles.

Step 2: Calculate Data Cache Stalls
Frequency of load/store instructions = $25\% = 0.25$
Data cache miss rate = $8\% = 0.08$
Data cache misses per instruction = $0.25 \times 0.08 = 0.02$
Data cache stall cycles per instruction = $0.02 \times 100 = 2$ cycles.

Step 3: Calculate Actual CPI
$\text{CPI}_{\text{actual}} = \text{Ideal CPI} + \text{Instruction Stall Cycles} + \text{Data Stall Cycles}$
$\text{CPI}_{\text{actual}} = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6$

Step 4: Calculate CPI with Perfect Cache
With a perfect cache, stall cycles = $0$.
$\text{CPI}_{\text{perfect}} = 2$

Step 5: Calculate Speedup
$\text{Speedup} = \frac{\text{CPI}_{\text{actual}}}{\text{CPI}_{\text{perfect}}} = \frac{6}{2} = 3$
